schema.name: analysis_inspect
schema.description: One-shot deep dive into a file or directory: symbols, definitions, references, call hierarchy and diagnostics, weighted by depth 1-5. Returns per-layer results plus a summary. Use it as the default entry point when you need to understand unfamiliar code. Next: analysis_architecture for a bird's-eye view.

depth.description:
Analysis depth:
  1: symbols + overview + diagnostics
  2: + capsule + callers + callees
  3: + call_hierarchy + type_hierarchy + highlight
  4: + cycle_detector + dependency_graph + hot_paths
  5: + blast_radius + unused_finder + complexity

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_report
schema.description: Assemble a structured analysis report from findings and recommendations, optionally persisting it. Returns the report document with finding and recommendation counts. Use it as the deliverable at the end of an analysis. Next: hand it to the user or export it.

schema.name: analysis_architecture
schema.description: Map a project: workspace structure, dependency graph, hot paths, import cycles, complexity hotspots. Returns apps/packages, top dependencies, cycle list and the most-imported files. Use it before a refactor or to explain a codebase. Next: analysis_inspect on the top-ranked files.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_deadcode
schema.description: Find code nothing uses: unused imports, unused functions, orphaned error handlers. Returns each category with file, line and symbol plus the total count. Use it for cleanup passes and before declaring a module stable. Next: code_safe_delete for confirmed dead symbols.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory to scan.

kinds.description: Dead code types: imports, functions, errors, all.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_performance
schema.description: Look for performance problems: complexity hotspots, diagnostics, hot paths, inlay hints. Returns ranked hotspots with complexity score and the files that dominate. Use it when something is slow or before adding load. Next: analysis_inspect with depth>=4 on the top hotspot.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_security
schema.description: Security pass: runs the security pattern catalogue and error-handling checks over a path. Returns findings with severity, file, line and the pattern that matched. Use it before a release or when reviewing untrusted-input handling. Next: analysis_review for diff context.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory to scan.

kinds.description: What kinds of issues to scan for (default: ['all']).

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_ask
schema.description: Ask a natural-language question about the codebase and answer it from stored analysis context. Returns the answer plus the evidence it used. Use it when you do not know which tool would answer the question. Next: run the concrete tool the answer points at.

question.description: A natural language question about the code.

schema.name: analysis_diff
schema.description: Compare two analysis reports and show what changed between them. Returns added, removed and worsened findings. Use it after a refactor to prove it did not regress. Next: analysis_report to write it up.

schema.name: analysis_trend
schema.description: Track how metrics developed across successive runs: finding counts, complexity, coverage. Returns a time series and the direction of change. Use it to show whether quality is improving over time. Next: analysis_report.

scope.description: Scope to analyze (e.g. 'path=src/', 'module:user-service'). Empty = all scopes.

intent.description: Filter by analysis intent. Empty = all intents.

schema.name: analysis_watch
schema.description: Watch a path and report changes since the last run, so repeated checks stay cheap. Returns newly added and resolved findings. Use it in a loop or a nightly job. Next: analysis_report for the delta summary.

frequency.description: Frequency: daily, hourly, or cron expr.

name.description: Watch name (required for remove). Auto-generated for create.

schema.name: analysis_graph
schema.description: Render analysis results as a Mermaid diagram: dependency graph, cycles or summary view. Returns Mermaid source ready to paste. Use it when a picture explains faster than a list. Next: analysis_report to embed it.

schema.name: analysis_ui_gap
schema.description: Compare backend capabilities with frontend usage to find endpoints the UI never calls. Returns the gap list with file references. Use it when a feature exists in the API but not in the product. Next: analysis_ui_inspect for the DOM side.

include_storefront.description: Include storefront routes in analysis (default: true).

include_admin.description: Include admin routes in analysis (default: true).

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_pattern_discover
schema.description: Find bug-shaped code that the shared pattern catalogue does not cover yet. Returns candidate patterns with evidence and a suggested scan query. Use it to grow the catalogue after a hunt found something new. Next: bug_hunt_pattern action=save to make it permanent.

path.description: Absolute path to the project or directory to scan.

schema.name: analysis_framework
schema.description: Identify the frameworks and tooling of a project with confidence scores. Returns each detected framework with version hints and evidence. Use it before choosing language-specific patterns. Next: bug_hunt_scan with the matching preset.

schema.name: analysis_dependency_risk
schema.description: Rate dependency risk for a file or project: outdated, unmaintained or heavily coupled dependencies. Returns a score per dependency with the reason. Use it when planning upgrades. Next: analysis_security for the code-level view.

schema.name: analysis_diff_analysis
schema.description: Compare two git refs and show which symbols changed, with complexity delta and blast radius. Returns changed functions per file plus an impact summary. Use it to review a branch before merging. Next: analysis_review for the security angle.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_risk
schema.description: Rate the risk of a change or a file: dependency risk, test coverage, blast radius. Returns a 0-10 score with the factors behind it. Use it to decide whether a change needs more testing. Next: code_tests_for_symbol to see what covers it.

categories.description: Risk categories to include (default: all). Options: dependencies, complexity, deadcode, security, hotspots, duplicates

schema.name: analysis_review
schema.description: Pre-commit style review: diff analysis plus review assistant plus a security pass. Returns changed functions, complexity deltas, security findings and suggested reviewers. Use it before opening a PR or before committing risky changes. Next: fix the findings, then re-run.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: analysis_test_insight
schema.description: Work out which tests cover a symbol, and optionally draft new ones. Returns covering test files ranked by relevance, plus generated test skeletons on request. Use it before changing untested code. Next: write the tests, then analysis_review.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory.

generate.description: Generate test scaffolds for untested symbols (default: false).

schema.name: analysis_ui_inspect
schema.description: Inspect rendered UI: DOM structure, selectors and accessibility issues for a route. Returns elements, selectors and findings. Use it when a frontend bug depends on the actual DOM rather than the source. Next: analysis_ui_gap for coverage.

store_baseline.description: Aktuellen Screenshot als Baseline speichern (fuer spaeteren Vergleich).

schema.name: bug_hunt_start
schema.description: Open a bug-hunt session for a project before you record anything. Creates a session record and returns session_id, scope and the finding count (0 at start); the session_id is required by every other bug-hunt tool. Use this first when the user asks to hunt bugs or run a security pass. Next: bug_hunt_scan for patterns, or bug_hunt_finding by hand.

schema.name: bug_hunt_finding
schema.description: Record one bug finding inside an existing session. Returns the new finding_id plus the session's updated finding count. Use it for each concrete defect you found by reading code; for pattern-based bulk scans use bug_hunt_scan instead, which creates findings automatically. Next: bug_hunt_triage or bug_hunt_report.

schema.name: bug_hunt_list
schema.description: List findings of a session, optionally filtered by severity, status, category or file. Returns matching findings (id, title, severity, status, file, line) plus a count. Use it to review what is recorded before adding duplicates, or to pick finding_ids for triage. Next: bug_hunt_triage or bug_hunt_report.

severity.description: Only findings with this severity (P0 highest .. INFO).

status.description: Only findings with this workflow status.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: bug_hunt_close
schema.description: Close a bug-hunt session and freeze it with a summary. Returns the closed session with its final finding statistics. Use it when the hunt is finished so the session stops accepting findings and appears correctly in bug_hunt_history. Next: bug_hunt_report for the deliverable.

schema.name: bug_hunt_scan
schema.description: Run the automated pattern scan against a project and create findings from matches. Returns patterns executed, matches found and findings created, per pattern. Use it after bug_hunt_start to cover the known-risk catalogue in one call instead of reading every file. Next: bug_hunt_list to inspect hits, bug_hunt_triage to sort signal from noise.

schema.name: bug_hunt_triage
schema.description: Classify findings: set a workflow status (triaged, false_positive, fixed, ...) and optionally re-rate severity. Returns the changed findings and the session's new status distribution. Use it to remove false positives before reporting, which is what makes a report trustworthy. Next: bug_hunt_report.

severity.description: Only findings with this severity (P0 highest .. INFO).

status.description: Only findings with this workflow status.

schema.name: bug_hunt_verify
schema.description: Mark findings as verified after you reproduced or confirmed them. Returns the verified findings and the remaining open count. Use it before closing a session so the report separates confirmed defects from unconfirmed ones. Next: bug_hunt_close.

schema.name: bug_hunt_fix
schema.description: Record that a finding was fixed, with the fix description and optional commit reference. Returns the updated finding with status fixed. Use it after applying the patch so the report shows what was resolved, not only what was found. Next: bug_hunt_report.

schema.name: bug_hunt_report
schema.description: Render the session report as markdown or JSON, optionally grouped by severity, category or file. Returns the formatted report plus counts per severity. Use it as the deliverable when the user asks for a summary of the hunt. Next: bug_hunt_export to write it to a file.

group_by.description: Group the report table by this key.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: bug_hunt_export
schema.description: Export a session report to a file on disk. Returns the absolute path, byte size and format of the written file. Use it when the report must survive the session or be handed to someone else. Next: research_save if the content belongs in the research archive.

schema.name: bug_hunt_history
schema.description: List past bug-hunt sessions with project, date, status and finding counts. Returns sessions newest first, optionally filtered by project or session. Use it to find an earlier hunt worth continuing, or to compare a codebase's defect count over time. Next: bug_hunt_list with a session_id from the result.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: bug_hunt_pattern
schema.description: Read or manage the pattern catalogue: list patterns, show one in detail, list categories, or save a new custom pattern from a confirmed finding. Returns patterns (id, name, category, severity, scan_type) or the saved pattern. Use it to see what the scanner checks, and to promote a manual bug into an automatic check. Next: bug_hunt_scan.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

pattern.description: Complete pattern definition, required for action=save. Fields: name, category, severity, description, scan_type, scan_query, scan_file_glob, scan_language, fix_description.

description.description: What the pattern detects and why it matters.

scan_query.description: Search expression used by the scanner.

scan_file_glob.description: File glob the scan applies to, e.g. **/*.ts.

schema.name: bug_hunt_stats
schema.description: Summarise a session: findings by severity, by status, by category and the top affected files. Returns the aggregate counts and the highest-risk files. Use it for a quick health read before writing the report, or to decide where to look next. Next: bug_hunt_report.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: research_start
schema.description: Open a research session and either plan it or run it end to end. mode=plan (default) returns research_id, the plan and step-by-step instructions; mode=auto executes search + parallel page reads + finding extraction and saves the result, returning research_id, findings, sources and gaps. Use it as the first call of any research task; pass schedule=24h for recurring monitoring. Next: research_export or research_status.

mode.description: plan returns a research plan plus next steps (the model drives the steps). auto runs the whole pass here — search, read, extract — and returns the findings with sources.

schedule.description: Optional interval (e.g. 24h, 7d) to register a recurring research run. Due runs are reported by research_schedule_due.

schema.name: research_save
schema.description: Store the result of a research session: summary, findings and sources. Returns the saved record with id, status and counts for findings and sources. Use it once you have read enough sources; every finding should carry the URL it came from, otherwise research_verify flags it. Next: research_export for a file, or research_synthesize across several results.

status.description: completed = answered, partial = gaps remain, failed = could not answer.

schema.name: research_cleanup
schema.description: Remove stale research artefacts: orphaned plans (started but never saved) or all leftover files. Returns the number of removed files per category. Use it before a release or when research_status reports orphans. Next: research_stats to confirm the store is tidy.

action.description: plans removes orphaned plans only, all removes every leftover artefact.

schema.name: research_update
schema.description: Modify, delete, tag, verify, merge or compare stored research results. action=patch (default) appends findings/sources or replaces summary and status and returns the updated record with new counts; delete returns the removed id; tag returns the record with its tags; verify returns the consistency problems found; merge returns the new result id; compare returns shared findings and contradictions. Use it to extend a finished session instead of starting a new one. Next: research_export.

status.description: completed = answered, partial = gaps remain, failed = could not answer.

action.description: patch (default) modifies summary/findings/sources; delete removes the result; tag add/remove/set/clear tags; verify checks source consistency; merge joins several results; compare contrasts two or more.

research_ids.description: Result ids for action=merge or action=compare.

append.description: Data to append to the stored result.

schema.name: research_search
schema.description: Full-text search across all stored research results (BM25 ranking, no external dependency). Returns matching results with id, query, summary excerpt and a relevance score. Use it to recall earlier research instead of repeating it. Next: research_status for details of a hit, or research_save to extend it.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: research_status
schema.description: Show the state of one research session, or list all sessions with their status. Returns the plan/result record including status (planned, completed, partial, failed), counts and timestamps. Use it to check whether a session was finished, and to find sessions started but never saved. Next: research_save to complete it.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: research_stats
schema.description: Aggregate numbers over the whole research store: sessions by status, total findings and sources, most used tags. Returns the aggregate counts. Use it to judge whether the store is worth searching before starting new research. Next: research_search to look inside it.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

schema.name: research_export
schema.description: Render one research result as markdown or plain text. Returns the formatted document plus its byte size. Use it when the user wants a readable write-up rather than a JSON record. Next: research_export_all for several results at once.

format.description: markdown keeps headings and lists, text is plain.

response_format.description: concise returns core fields only (~1/3 of the tokens); detailed returns everything.

all.description: Export every stored result into one document instead of one id.

schema.name: research_synthesize
schema.description: Build a cross-cutting answer from several stored research results. Returns the matching local results and an instruction block for combining them with honcho_reasoning. Use it when the user asks what the research collectively says, not for a single result. Next: research_merge if the combined answer should become one record.
